title: Anchoring with the senses
header_line: My analysis of one book on negotiation. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What do you want them to associate with you?
I asked the class: what is anchoring, and what is the power of anchoring?

I gave the example of a student who asked a client to think of the most beautiful object they had ever seen, which becomes an anchor, because they then associate it with the design she will make for them.
A student said that using the words trust or credibility, as in people who know me know I am always going to do them right, creates comfort.
I said that you can practice until everything you say, such as get home now, has that kind of power, and that emotions are like tickets on a shelf: anger, frustration, happiness.
I said that what drives consciousness, memories and anchors is the senses, not only a thought process: for example a perfume you wear into a meeting.
I said that a person responds to their own map of reality, and that you cannot only look at the map; you have to look at the colors that painted it, their emotional and belief experiences.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the anchor you want clients to hold.
Write the words you will use.
Write the sense you will add: sound, scent or image.
Write one person's map and its colors.
Write how patient you will be.

check.q: What did I say drives anchors?
What did a student say creates comfort?
What did I say to look at besides the map?

recap: Anchor with words and senses. Look at the colors that painted their map.
